# `silk/time/zones_native`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

The system providers of the `TimeZones` and `LocalZone` effects: the time zone database and
the zone setting of the operating system.

## When to use
Provide [`OsTimeZones`](#OsTimeZones) for `TimeZones` and [`OsLocalZone`](#OsLocalZone) for `LocalZone` in a program that
shows local times. In a test, provide `FixedTimeZones` and `FixedLocalZone` of
`silk.time.zones`, so the result does not depend on the machine.

## Details
Each operating system has its own implementation behind these two providers, and a program
names no path and no system call. On Linux and macOS, the zones are the TZif files of the
system: the directory that the variable `TZDIR` names, then `/usr/share/zoneinfo` and the
other usual places. The local zone is the variable `TZ`, then the link `/etc/localtime`, then
the file `/etc/timezone`.

A zone is read from its file at each lookup. Load a zone one time and keep it.

## Gotchas
- A minimal container image often has no zone files. Then each lookup fails with the reason
  `UnknownZone`, except for `UTC` and fixed offsets, which need no data.
- The zones change when the operating system updates its database, so two machines can
  disagree about a future date.
- `OsLocalZone` can return a `TZ` value that is a POSIX rule, such as `EST5EDT,M3.2.0,M11.1.0`,
  and not a zone name. `OsTimeZones` gives the zone for such a rule too.
- The providers exist on Darwin x86_64 or aarch64 and on GNU Linux x86_64 or aarch64.

## Examples
### Show an instant in the zone of this machine
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.collections.bytes { Bytes }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.time.instant { Instant }
import silk.time.zoned { ZonedDateTime }
import silk.time.zones { LocalZone, NoLocalZoneError, TimeZones, ZoneLookupError }
import silk.time.zones_native { OsLocalZone, OsTimeZones }

effect fn localYear(at: Instant) -> i32
  ! ZoneLookupError | NoLocalZoneError | OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut TimeZones | &mut LocalZone | &mut Allocator {
  let name = run LocalZone.name()
  let zone = run TimeZones.zoneBytes(Bytes.asSlice(&name))
  return ZonedDateTime.make(at, &zone).date().year()
}

// A machine without a zone setting or without zone files is not an error of this example.
effect fn missing(error: ZoneLookupError | NoLocalZoneError | OutOfMemoryError) -> i32 {
  return 2026
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let mut zones = OsTimeZones.make()
  let mut here = OsLocalZone.make()
  let year = run Effect.catchAll(localYear(Instant.fromUnixSeconds(1795109782)), missing)
    |> Effect.provideMut<TimeZones>(&mut zones)
    |> Effect.provideMut<LocalZone>(&mut here)
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  if year != 2026 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `OsTimeZones` with `import silk.time.zones_native { OsTimeZones }`.

```silk
pub struct OsTimeZones
```

The system `TimeZones` provider: the time zone database of the operating system. It has no
state.

### Gotchas
- A machine without zone files fails each lookup with the reason `UnknownZone`, except for
  `UTC` and fixed offsets.

## `OsLocalZone`

```silk
pub struct OsLocalZone
```

The system `LocalZone` provider: the zone that this machine is set to. It has no state.

### Gotchas
- The answer can be a POSIX rule from the variable `TZ`, not a zone name.
